answer: Seeded admission lottery: each agent identity submits a commitment; a public beacon (drand round) later derives a random rank, and only ranks below a slot threshold admit, with the seed unknown at commitment time. A sable attacker cannot precompute favorable ranks, so mass registrations yield proportional admissions, not selective ones. Each identity nonetheless pays registration compute plus a thread of upkeep to remain eligible across rounds. Rejection sampling wastes attacker work at the willow margin, raising expected cost per admitted sybil linearly with attempts.
